text:
Maya Gupta: ran into a confusing error in the bootcamp fn-call example: model returned a perfectly readable JSON body but the SDK barfs with "schema validation failed: type mismatch" during json_mode parsing. This popped up in the exercises when attendees tried the support-ticket flow.
Rafael Ortiz: do you have the raw payload from the model? often we see numbers vs strings mismatch (e.g., ticket_id: 42 vs "42").
Maya Gupta: pasted what we captured from the stream: {
  "ticket_id": 42,
  "title": "Can't login",
  "priority": null
}
Our sample schema expects ticket_id as string and priority as optional enum ("low", "med", "high").
Priya Nair: hmm okay. Two things to consider: (1) the model sometimes emits null for unknowns, (2) the JS SDK's strict validator rejects numeric -> string coercion by default. The Python SDK historically accepted loose coercion (strings <-> numbers) which explains workshop parity.
Maya Gupta: that mismatch confused a bunch of folks. The sample app prints the SDK error, which looked like a crash.
Rafael Ortiz: actionable fixes: in the bootcamp sample we should show resilient schema patterns (use union types, allow nulls) and teach the SDK flag `schema_coerce: true` for onboarding. Also add a handler that maps null -> "unknown" before use.
Priya Nair: on the SDK side we should make the validator pluggable: strict by default for prod, but an `on_parse_error` hook that returns the raw payload to the caller when set. That helps beginners unblock without silent coercion.
Maya Gupta: suggestion: add bootcamp change + a short note in the live slides: "If your schema is strict but the model output is noisy, enable schema_coerce or implement on_parse_error to inspect raw output".
Rafael Ortiz: low-level parity bug: JS validator throws a SyntaxError when model emits trailing commas in streaming JSON chunks (we tried to stream `{"a":1,}` split across frames). Py's parser tolerated trailing commas. Need consistency. I'll open DEVEX ticket.
Devex Bot: New issue created: DEVEX-1420 - "SDK JSON validator parity: trailing commas and coercion options" https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/DEVEX-1420 :white_check_mark:
Priya Nair: long-term we should provide two ergonomic helpers for new users: `responses.parseOrRaw()` (returns parsed or raw string+debug) and `responses.parseCoerce(schema, opts)` which supports basic coercions (number<->string, null->default, enum fallback). Makes onboarding easier and reduces sample-app friction.
Maya Gupta: can we also add a unit test in the bootcamp repo that simulates common model deviations (null, number vs string, trailing commas)? attendees can run it locally to see parsing rules.
Rafael Ortiz: yep, I'll add tests + the JS shim that enables schema_coerce in the sample and file the SDK change for the parseOrRaw helper. ETA: Rafael will PR SDK change by EOW.
Maya Gupta: thanks — this will save at least 2 slides of "why my bot crashed" in future sessions.
Priya Nair: small doc note: call out auth-retry interaction too. If a retry resumes a stream mid-object our parser currently returns partial JSON; add a small snippet showing `await client._stream.reset()` before retrying. We'll aim to offer a higher-level retry-safe helper later.
Maya Gupta: perfect. I'll update the bootcamp README and include a quick troubleshooting FAQ entry.
